design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated after cardiac surgery using a computer-generated 1:1:2 randomization code to two epoetin-dose groups or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and baseline characteristics were balanced, but allocation used envelopes whose opacity, sequential numbering, and tamper-proof handling were not described, leaving some uncertainty about concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomization code was generated by a computer 1:1:2 and envelopes with allocation were prepared by the quality of care unit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and investigators/care-takers were blinded, injections were prepared by a separate nurse, all randomized patients were retained, and no intervention-related deviations affecting outcomes were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A nurse from the Nephrology Unit opened the envelopes and prepared the syringes for injection. Investigators and patients were blinded to the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for nearly all randomized participants; only one patient transferred at 48 hours lacked complete biological follow-up, making material bias from missingness unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only 1 patient was transferred in another hospital at 48 h. Although we could not have the complete biological follow-up, we could have the information that he did not develop AKI and was alive.

domain_judgments.rationale: The prespecified primary outcome was measured using a standardized commercial assay at fixed times, samples were processed together, and blinded assignment reduced the potential for differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Rapid NGAL ELISA kit (Bioport Diagnostics-Gentofte, Denmark) was used to measure urinary NGAL (uNGAL) ... All samples for NGAL and cytokines measures were processed at the same time.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and its primary outcome identified, but the text does not establish a prospectively finalized analysis plan and reports both three-group and post hoc pooled-dose analyses among several outcomes and time points, allowing some analytical flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We pooled the two EPO doses and confirmed that r-HuEPO did not significantly modify uNGAL median levels between 48 hours and randomization.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of envelope-based allocation concealment and uncertainty about prospective specification of the analyses, including pooling of the two active-dose groups. Missing data and outcome measurement present low risk, with effective blinding and nearly complete follow-up.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 blocked randomization of participants to rHuEPO or saline placebo, with allocation revealed from sealed envelopes after recruitment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blocked randomization and sealed-envelope allocation were reported, and measured baseline characteristics were comparable, but the method used to generate the random sequence and safeguards such as opaque, sequentially numbered envelopes were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment assignment among the two groups was determined by blocked randomization. After recruitment, three days before the operation, sealed envelopes containing the allocation group were opened by nurses who did not participate in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators were blinded and identical preparations were used, with no important intervention-related deviations reported, but two randomized participants were excluded after allocation and no explicit intention-to-treat analysis was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients and investigators were also blinded to group assignment. Pairs of identical 0.3 ml syringes containing either rHuEPO (5,000 U, Recormon, Roche) or saline were prepared and stored.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only two of 102 randomized participants were excluded, one per group for reasons occurring before treatment, and primary outcome data were reported for all 100 participants who received assigned treatment, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One patient in the rHuEPO and one from the placebo group were excluded because of the lack of medical treatment and a CABG cancelation. Consequently, 100 patients received their assigned treatments to the placebo (n = 50) or rHuEPO (n = 50) group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome used a prespecified objective KDIGO serum-creatinine definition, laboratory testing was standardized across groups, and participants and investigators were blinded, making differential outcome measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The definition of CSA-AKI is defined as a ≥ 0.3 mg/dl or ≥ 50% increase in SCr levels from baseline within the first 48 hr post-operation according to the newer criteria of AKI from KDIGO guideline 2012.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and endpoints were identified, but the provided report does not establish that a prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan fixed all outcome time points and analyses before unblinded data were available, despite multiple renal measures and time-point comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered in the Protocol Registration System (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01066351).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. This is driven by incomplete reporting of sequence generation and allocation-concealment safeguards, post-randomization exclusion without an explicit intention-to-treat analysis, and insufficient information to rule out selective reporting; missing data and objective blinded outcome measurement were otherwise unlikely to cause important bias.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that patients were randomized to darbepoetin alfa or placebo using an Internet-based centralized system, with stratification by sex, age, center, and cancer location.

domain_judgments.rationale: Centralized Internet-based randomization by authorized secretaries, stratification on key prognostic variables, maintained blinding, and similar baseline characteristics support an adequately concealed randomization process, although the exact sequence-generation algorithm is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization to study treatment was performed by authorized secretaries via an Internet homepage ... and was stratified by sex, age (above or below 70 years), center and cancer localization (colon or rectum).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators remained blinded, emergency codes were never broken, treatment was protocolized, and the authors report intention-to-treat analysis according to a preestablished plan, making bias from intervention deviations unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times. Code-breaking sheets for emergency use were available but were never used.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 151 of 202 randomized patients completed the study, with 30 post-randomization exclusions and 17 additional dropouts; the reported efficacy-valid population therefore omitted about one quarter of randomized participants without analyses demonstrating that missingness could not bias the outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 221 patients were enrolled into the study, of whom 202 patients were randomized and 151 completed the study (efficacy-valid population).

domain_judgments.rationale: Physical-performance outcomes were assessed with prespecified standardized instruments and procedures applied equally across groups, while participant and investigator blinding reduced the chance that knowledge of allocation influenced measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors mention a preestablished analysis plan and identify the principal time point, but no protocol or registration is provided, multiple physical outcomes and time points were tested, and no multiplicity correction was used, leaving scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were entered before treatment codes were broken and analyzed on an intent-totreat basis according to a preestablished analysis plan. ... No correction for multiple testing was made.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because outcome data were available for only 151 of 202 randomized participants and the efficacy-valid analysis excluded substantial post-randomization losses without evidence that missingness was non-biasing. There are also some concerns about selective reporting given multiple outcomes and time points without an accessible protocol or multiplicity correction.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports a prospective randomized trial using a centrally generated, stratified block-randomization list with 1:1 allocation through an Internet system.

domain_judgments.rationale: A centrally generated stratified block-randomization list and Internet-based allocation provided an adequately random and concealed sequence, and observed baseline differences were compatible with chance in this small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomization code list with a block size of two was generated by Medical Research Collaborating Center Seoul National University Hospital... Treatments were allocated to patients through the Internet in accordance with the predefined randomization list (1:1 ratio for EPO or placebo group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients, clinicians, and investigators were blinded, placebo administration matched the active intervention, all randomized participants completed the trial, and no intervention-related deviations likely to affect outcomes were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients, healthcare clinicians, and investigators were blinded to treatment assignment... 71 patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 36) or saline (n = 35) and completed this trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for all 71 randomized patients, with no reported loss to follow-up through the five-day outcome period.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 71 patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 36) or saline (n = 35) and completed this trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: AKI was defined prospectively using objective serial serum-creatinine measurements obtained at the same scheduled times in both groups, and investigators were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blood samples for SCr determination were obtained preoperatively (‘baseline’) and at postoperative 24, 72, and 120 h... The primary endpoint was the incidence of AKI after CABG, defined as a 50% increase in SCr levels from baseline at any time within the first 5 postoperative days.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the primary endpoint was clearly defined, but the text does not establish prospective registration or provide a protocol/statistical analysis plan sufficient to exclude selective reporting among multiple renal measurements and time-point analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (www.clinicaltrial.gov), No. NCT 00654992.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by insufficient information to rule out selective reporting despite trial registration and a clearly stated primary outcome. Randomization, blinding, completeness of outcome data, and objective outcome measurement were otherwise adequately described.

design_rationale: The trial explicitly states that 74 patients were allocated 1:1 using computer-generated random numbers, with randomization and assignment performed by a ward physician not otherwise involved in the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated by an independent ward physician and observed baseline characteristics were broadly similar, but the report does not clearly describe how the sequence was concealed before enrollment and assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly allocated to either the rHuEPO or the control group in a 1:1 ratio by means of computer-generated random numbers. A ward physician not involved in the current trial performed randomization and assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and the clinical surgeon and anesthesiologist were blinded with a saline control, treatment delivery was standardized, and all randomized patients were analyzed in their assigned groups with no reported intervention-related deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients in the control group received an equivalent volume of normal saline for the same duration without iron supplementation... the surgeon and anesthesiologist involved in the study and patient management were blinded to the patients’ groups until the end of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were complete for all 74 randomized participants, making bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: VHS could be performed as planned in all patients, and complete data sets from the 74 patients were analyzed without any missing data.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary transfusion outcome was objectively recorded using prespecified hemoglobin thresholds and identical monitoring across groups, while the clinicians managing transfusion were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hemoglobin concentration less than 7 mg/dl during CPB, and less than 8 mg/dl after CPB and postoperatively, were used as transfusion thresholds.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes and analyses are described, but no prospectively registered protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is cited, and numerous outcome measurements and time points leave some potential for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary endpoints were comparisons of perioperative transfusion requirement in terms of overall incidence and mean number of units of packed erythrocytes transfused per patient during the operation and for 4 PODs.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of allocation concealment and the absence of a cited prospective registration or prespecified analysis plan. Blinding, complete outcome data, objective transfusion criteria, and analysis of all randomized participants otherwise support low risk across the remaining domains.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized to weekly subcutaneous erythropoietin or saline placebo in the multicenter EPO-TBI randomized controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is explicit, but this report defers the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods to an earlier publication and provides no treatment-group baseline comparison, so the adequacy of the process cannot be fully verified here.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomization process and administration of drug has been described previously.

domain_judgments.rationale: The parent trial was double-blind, used a saline placebo, and analyzed 603 of 606 randomized participants with only three consent withdrawals, with no reported intervention-related deviations likely to affect the renal outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Enrolled patients received either weekly doses of 40 000 IU of subcutaneous epoetin alfa (Eprex Janssen‐Cilag Pty Ltd, Titusville, NJ, USA) or placebo (0.9% sodium chloride).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome analysis included 603 of 606 randomized patients, with the only exclusions being three consent withdrawals, making bias from missing participant outcome data unlikely, although urinary-output follow-up was intentionally limited to seven days.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Consent was withdrawn in three patients; therefore, this analysis included a total of 603 patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: AKI was measured prospectively and consistently across groups using objective serum creatinine, urinary-output, and renal-replacement-therapy criteria defined by KDIGO, so knowledge of assignment was unlikely to influence measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Serum creatinine was prospectively recorded daily until ICU discharge and urine output during the first 7 days.

domain_judgments.rationale: The renal substudy is described as pre-planned and the parent trial was registered with a statistical analysis plan, but the text inconsistently labels the analysis as pre-planned and post hoc and reports several AKI definitions, time windows, and analyses without enough supplied protocol detail to rule out selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The EPO‐AKI sub‐study was a pre‐planned study and the protocol (a part of the original EPO‐AKI protocol) is included in the Supplementary Materials.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Objective, prospectively collected AKI outcomes were nearly complete in a placebo-controlled, double-blind RCT, but this report does not provide enough detail on sequence generation/allocation concealment and leaves some uncertainty about selective reporting across multiple renal outcome definitions and analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated 1:1 using simple randomization based on a computer-generated random code.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and baseline characteristics were broadly similar, but the report does not state how the allocation sequence was concealed before assignment; the diabetes imbalance could plausibly reflect chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly allocated to either the EPO or control group in a 1:1 ratio according to simple randomization using a computer-generated random code.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients received matched intravenous EPO or saline after induction under double-blind conditions, perioperative management was standardized, the unblinded medication-preparing nurse had no study role, and all randomized patients were analyzed in their assigned groups with no dropout.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients in the control group received an equal volume of normal saline at the same time point. Medications were prepared by a nurse who knew the patient’s group assignment but was not involved in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data appear available for all 98 randomized participants, with the authors explicitly reporting no post-allocation dropout.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of ninety-eight patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 49) or normal saline (n = 49), and no patient was dropped out after group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: AKI was defined prospectively using objective serum-creatinine-based AKIN criteria and measured identically across groups, making differential assessment unlikely despite incomplete detail about assessor blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint of interest was incidence of AKI, which was diagnosed according to the Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN) criteria (absolute increase in the sCr concentration ≥0.3 mg/dL from baseline or ≥50% increase in the sCr concentration within 48 hours after operation).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the primary endpoint and statistical methods are clearly described, but the text does not establish prospective registration or availability of a protocol/statistical analysis plan sufficient to rule out selection among multiple outcomes or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This single-site trial was conducted at Yonsei University Health System, Seoul, Korea (Clinical-Trials.gov NCT0178861).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by unreported allocation concealment and insufficient information to exclude selective reporting despite trial registration. Missing data, deviations from intervention, and objective outcome measurement were at low risk.

design_rationale: The study used an uncontrolled before-after audit of ICU prescriptions, with new procedures introduced between audit rounds and no explicit random allocation of participants or prescriptions to conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The uncontrolled before-after comparison is highly vulnerable to secular changes, differences in patients, drugs, prescribers, and workload between the two audit periods, and no confounder measurement or adjustment was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: New procedures were introduced, which included a standardised prescription sticker, with common, preprinted, infusion prescriptions on (noradrenaline, propofol, and so forth), and education on using the new prescription stickers. A month later the audit process was repeated.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Although all patients' daily infusion charts were reportedly audited during each set of spot checks, the short spot-check periods and absence of information on patient comparability or exclusions leave plausible selection differences between periods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We audited the daily infusion charts of all patients in three separate spot checks, over 1 week.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intervention status was clearly distinguished by calendar period and the intervention components were explicitly described, making misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: New procedures were introduced, which included a standardised prescription sticker, with common, preprinted, infusion prescriptions on (noradrenaline, propofol, and so forth), and education on using the new prescription stickers. A month later the audit process was repeated.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract does not report intervention fidelity, uptake of the stickers and education, co-interventions, or an analysis accounting for deviations, so deviations from intended practice cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: New procedures were introduced, which included a standardised prescription sticker, with common, preprinted, infusion prescriptions on (noradrenaline, propofol, and so forth), and education on using the new prescription stickers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Prescription counts are reported for both rounds, but there is no accounting of eligible prescriptions or charts, exclusions, unavailable records, or missing outcome fields, so completeness cannot be established.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We assessed 129 prescriptions in the first round, and 111 after intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome criteria were based on national guidance and appear consistently applicable, but assessor blinding, reliability, and detailed measurement procedures were not reported, allowing knowledge of the post-intervention period to influence judgments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We assessed all aspects of prescriptions that make them legal and valid, in accordance with national guidance.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol, preregistration, or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and several possible prescribing outcomes could have been selected for presentation after analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only 24% of prescriptions initially fulfilled best practice criteria, improving to 94% afterwards. We also reduced the number of infusions running without prescription, 7 (6%) versus 24 (19%).

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven by the uncontrolled before-after design and lack of control for secular and case-mix confounding. Additional moderate concerns arise from incomplete reporting of selection, intervention fidelity, missing data, assessor blinding, and prespecification of outcomes and analyses.

design_rationale: The parent Epo-ACR-02 trial explicitly randomly assigned eligible patients 1:1 to erythropoietin or control, stratified by site; this report is a post hoc single-centre subgroup analysis of that randomized trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random 1:1 assignment stratified by site is stated and measured baseline characteristics were broadly similar, but the sequence-generation method and allocation concealment are not reported in this article.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After being screened for eligibility, patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or to the control group. Intervention assignments were stratified by site.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label and some Epo participants did not receive all five injections, while the post-randomization exclusions and available-case analyses do not constitute a clear intention-to-treat analysis, although ICU co-interventions were reportedly similar.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, the Epo-ACR-02 study was an open-label trial while this study is a single-centre trial on a small sample of patients with an exploratory design, which limits generalization of our results.

domain_judgments.rationale: The analysis excluded 50 of 212 randomized patients after allocation, including 43 who died within 24 hours, and the primary endpoint was additionally unavailable for 7 of 162 analyzed patients; exclusion based on early death could plausibly depend on prognosis and distort the estimated intervention effect on AKI.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Five patients with CKD in the Epo group and 2 in the control group were excluded, as 21 patients in the Epo group and 22 in the control group died within the first 24 h after ICU admission.

domain_judgments.rationale: AKI was measured consistently using prespecified KDIGO-based criteria, but baseline creatinine was imputed by back-calculation for every patient, RRT and urine-output criteria may not specifically reflect renal injury, and the open-label design leaves unclear whether outcome classification or RRT decisions were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For all analysed patients, pre-CA creatinine was back-calculated through the Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) equation assuming a 75 mL/min/1.73 m2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), as recommended.

domain_judgments.rationale: Renal outcomes were explored post hoc without a reported prespecified protocol or analysis plan, and numerous alternative AKI definitions, time points, and analyses create substantial opportunity to select among eligible results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We therefore aimed to explore, post hoc, in a subgroup of the Epo-ACR-02 trial population, whether there are any renoprotective effects of Epo therapy on patients with resuscitated CA.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by extensive post-randomization exclusions—especially early deaths—and the post hoc, exploratory selection of renal outcomes and analyses without a reported prespecified plan. Additional concerns arise from incomplete reporting of allocation concealment, open-label treatment, and aspects of AKI measurement.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports computer-generated random allocation by an independent investigator to erythropoietin or saline.

domain_judgments.rationale: An independent investigator used a computer-generated sequence and handled assignment and solution preparation, while all clinical and analytic personnel remained blinded; the isolated sex imbalance is compatible with chance in this small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent investigator performed computer-generated randomization, enrolled patients, and assigned patients to the erythropoietin group or the control group. He also prepared all drug solutions and provided them to the anesthesia practitioner.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding and standardized perioperative care make intervention-related deviations unlikely, but six randomized participants were excluded from the final analysis and an intention-to-treat analysis is not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The anesthetic administrator, surgeons, patients, outcome assessors, and data analysts were all blinded to patient allocations throughout the entire study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome analysis included 60 of 66 enrolled participants (90.9%), but the provided text does not report the reasons or group allocation for the six exclusions, so bias from missing outcomes cannot be ruled out.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 66 patients enrolled, 60 patients were included in the final analysis (Fig 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: AKI was measured in both groups using prespecified objective serum-creatinine-based RIFLE criteria over seven days, and outcome assessors were blinded; omission of imprecise urine-output data was applied consistently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the incidence of AKI according to the RIFLE criteria... The anesthetic administrator, surgeons, patients, outcome assessors, and data analysts were all blinded to patient allocations throughout the entire study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint and analysis approach are described, but no prospective protocol, registration, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported to exclude selective choice among multiple renal measurements and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the incidence of AKI according to the RIFLE criteria (acronym for risk, injury, failure, loss of function, and end-stage renal disease).

overall_summary: The trial had sound computer-generated randomization, extensive blinding, and objective outcome measurement. Overall risk nevertheless has some concerns because 6 of 66 randomized/enrolled participants were omitted without reasons or reported intention-to-treat analysis, and prospective registration or an analysis protocol was not reported.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized 1:1 to recombinant human erythropoietin or placebo within 24 hours of birth, with stratification by gestational age, multiple birth, and site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment, stratification, and balanced baseline characteristics are reported, but the sequence-generation method and allocation-concealment mechanism are not described in this report.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization allocation was 1:1, with patients stratified by gestational age category, multiple births, and study site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Families and study personnel were blinded, placebo/sham procedures paralleled active treatment, and no intervention-related deviations likely to affect outcomes were reported, although a formal intention-to-treat label was not given.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subjects received rhEpo at a dose of 1000 units/kg or placebo intravenously every 48 hours for a total of 6 doses; thereafter participants received either 400 U/kg/dose rhEpo subcutaneously or sham injections 3 times a week until they reached 32 6/7 weeks of cGA. Study personnel and families were still blinded to randomization groups at the follow-up visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Long-term kidney outcomes were available for only subsets of randomized participants, with differential loss to follow-up and potentially outcome-related differences among those missing blood pressure; short-term AKI also classified 23 infants without creatinine values as having no AKI.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We also acknowledge that a large number of patients did not have kidney-related metrics measured at the 2-year cGA time point.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured consistently under blinded assignment, including core-laboratory assays and standardized blood-pressure procedures, but clinical creatinine testing varied by site and the authors state that several long-term measurements were not gold-standard assessments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: First, not all neonates had SCr captured every day during the hospitalization; therefore, it is possible that the true AKI rate could be greater. Second, we acknowledge that although we performed studyrelated measurements that were optimized for a one-time visit, the methods to capture kidney-related outcomes (eGFR, spot urine ACR, and one-time manual blood pressure measurements) are not gold-standard methods to assess kidney-related outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The severe-AKI outcome was described as a priori and measurement time points were predetermined, but no kidney-specific prespecified analysis plan is presented and numerous outcomes, thresholds, adjusted analyses, and alternative blood-pressure summaries leave scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our a priori primary short-term outcome was severe AKI any time during the hospitalization.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by extensive and partly differential missing outcome data for the 22-26-month kidney and blood-pressure outcomes, with plausible selection related to outcome. Additional concerns arise from incompletely reported allocation methods, non-gold-standard outcome ascertainment, and analysis/reporting flexibility.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used computer-generated randomization tables to allocate 320 eligible patients to erythropoietin or control, with the next table value concealed until enrollment.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated allocation table was used, the next assignment was concealed until an eligible patient enrolled, and extensive baseline characteristics were broadly balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A custom simple application running in Windows XP (Microsoft Corp, Redmond, WA) was used to obtain randomization tables, and the next value of the table was kept secret until a suitable patient was enrolled.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and clinical staff knew treatment assignment in this open-treatment comparison, creating potential for differential care, although co-interventions and transfusion criteria were standardized and all randomized patients were analyzed by intention to treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients, nurses, and ward physician knew whether HRE was being administered or not, but the investigators did not... Two patients in the HRE group and 1 patient in the control group were converted to on-pump revascularization. These patients were considered as intention-to-treat and were therefore included in the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 320 randomized participants appear to have been retained in the intention-to-treat analysis, with no reported loss of primary transfusion or day-4 hemoglobin outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the remaining 320 patients, 158 were allocated to HRE administration and all received the intended treatment; 162 were allocated to the control group... These patients were considered as intention-to-treat and were therefore included in the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objectively documented transfusion under the same prespecified hemoglobin trigger in both groups, hemoglobin was measured automatically by the central laboratory, and investigators collecting outcomes were blinded and unable to influence transfusion decisions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Transfusion need was triggered by Hb levels less than 8.0 g/dL, and the same criteria were applied to both groups. Hb values were automatically collected by the central laboratory computer.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes were prespecified in the article, but no prospective protocol or trial registration is reported, and several statistical techniques and ancillary/subgroup analyses leave some potential for selective analysis or reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was the need for allogenic transfusion. The secondary end point was the Hb value on postoperative day 4. Ancillary objectives were the Hb trend from baseline to day 4 with and without HRE administration, and the cost-effectiveness of HRE versus the reduced need for transfusion.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization, outcome completeness, and objective measurement were strong, but knowledge of assignment by patients and treating staff could have influenced care, and the absence of a reported prospective protocol or registration leaves potential for selective result reporting.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized to rHuEPO or placebo using site-stratified, computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and stratified by site, with generally balanced groups, but the report does not explicitly describe allocation concealment before assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was stratified by site and entailed use of computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were blinded with an appearance-matched placebo, treatment rules were prespecified, and outcomes were analyzed by intention to treat, with no reported intervention-related deviations likely to bias the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study drug (40000 units of rHuEPO [Procrit; Ortho Biotech Products, LP, Bridgewater, NJ] ) or a placebo identical in appearance was administered by subcutaneous injection... Analysis of outcomes was on an intent-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: All randomized patients were included in the primary analysis, and the conservative sensitivity analysis classifying withdrawn or lost participants as transfused produced a similar estimate, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients not receiving transfusion at the time of study withdrawal or lost to follow-up were considered not transfused for this analysis. In addition, a second analysis was done in which all patients withdrawn or lost to follow-up were considered transfused.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of any RBC transfusion was objective and recorded consistently, while double blinding and similar pretransfusion hemoglobin values reduced the possibility that treatment knowledge influenced physicians' transfusion decisions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy end point was transfusion independence, assessed by comparing the percentage of patients in each treatment group who received any RBC transfusion between study days 1 and 28.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes were prospectively identified and secondary analyses were protocol-specified, but no publicly accessible preregistration or full protocol/statistical analysis plan is provided to exclude selection among eligible measurements or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Secondary efficacy end points identified prospectively were cumulative RBC units transfused per patient through study day 28; cumulative mortality through study day 28; change in hemoglobin from baseline; and time to first transfusion or death.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by absent explicit reporting of allocation concealment and the lack of a publicly accessible preregistration or complete protocol/analysis plan. Blinding, intention-to-treat analysis, objective outcome measurement, and missing-data sensitivity analyses otherwise support low risk.

design_rationale: The intervention trial explicitly used a predefined computer-generated randomization sequence with permuted blocks, stratified by center, to allocate eligible patients 1:1 to erythropoietin or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with permuted blocks and center stratification, concealment was maintained by a pharmacist using identical prepared syringes, and the observed baseline imbalances were plausibly due to chance and did not affect adjusted results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible patients were allocated to EPO or placebo (normal saline) groups in a 1:1 ratio, using a predefined computer-generated randomization sequence with permuted blocks stratified on center. Concealment was by pharmacist; pairs of identical 5-ml syringes containing EPO (50 000 U in 3 ml) or normal saline were prepared and stored.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, clinicians, and investigators were masked; all randomized participants received at least one dose; and the primary efficacy analysis used the intention-to-treat population, making bias from deviations unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients, all medical staff, and investigators were masked to treatment... The primary outcome and safety endpoints were evaluated in the ITT population... As all randomized patients had received at least one dose of the study medication; the ITT and safety populations were identical.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary ITT analysis included all 162 randomized participants (78 placebo and 84 EPO), with outcome calculation specified through the last measurement before death or day 7, so primary-outcome data appear essentially complete.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcome ITT population (n=78) [placebo] (n=84) [EPO]... RAVC was calculated using the trapezoidal rule to estimate the incremental area above baseline from the first value in the ICU (time 0) to the last measure before death or on day 7 (time t).

domain_judgments.rationale: The prospectively defined primary outcome was based on objective laboratory plasma-creatinine measurements collected under the same protocol, and treatment masking minimized differential measurement or assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The prospectively defined primary outcome was the RAVC, defined as the average pCr (pC) increase from baseline... Patients, all medical staff, and investigators were masked to treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome and secondary outcomes were described as prospectively defined and the trial was registered, but no accessible protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided to exclude selection among multiple analyses, baseline-creatinine rules, and subgroup or secondary-outcome results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the multiregional ethics committee of New Zealand (MEC/050020029) and registered under the Australian Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN012606000058572)... The prospectively defined primary outcome was the RAVC.

overall_summary: The trial had robust randomization and concealment, comprehensive blinding, ITT analysis with essentially complete primary-outcome data, and objective outcome measurement. Overall risk is some concerns because the available report and registry statement do not fully exclude selective reporting among multiple eligible analyses and outcome specifications.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 allocation using permuted-block randomization, with 138 patients randomized to EPO or saline control.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random permuted-block sequence and central randomization were reported, treatment assignment was blinded, and measured baseline characteristics were well balanced, with no indication of a randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible patients were allocated to EPO ... or standard preventive protocol only in a 1:1 ratio, using a permuted block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and the interventional cardiologist were blinded using a saline control, and co-interventions were standardized, but blinding of other care staff and an explicit intention-to-treat analysis were not reported; nevertheless, all randomized patients appear included in the primary analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients and the interventional cardiologist were blinded to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary CIN outcome was reported for all 138 randomized patients, although secondary biomarker data were missing for 40 patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: CIN occurred in 12 of the 138 patients (8.7%).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective laboratory endpoint defined prospectively and measured at the same specified times in both groups, making influence from knowledge of treatment unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Scr post CA was measured at 24 and 48 h post-procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the stated primary endpoint was reported, but the text does not establish prospective registration or provide a protocol/statistical analysis plan sufficient to rule out selection among eligible analyses or outcome definitions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (www.clinicaltrial.gov), No. NCT01364402.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of allocation concealment/analysis population details and insufficient information to exclude selective reporting. The primary outcome itself was objective, measured consistently, and available for all randomized participants.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports central, center-stratified allocation using a computer-generated randomization code to assign patients to two Epoetin alfa doses or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated, center-stratified sequence and central registration were reported, with balanced baseline characteristics, but the report does not explicitly state that the allocation sequence was concealed until assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were registered centrally, stratified by center, and randomized before scheduled operation to receive either Epoetin alfa or placebo on the basis of a computer-generated randomization code.

domain_judgments.rationale: Study medication identity was blinded and cointerventions and transfusion policy were broadly standardized, but administered volume was visible to investigators and the primary efficacy analysis excluded some randomized participants, although a modified intent-to-treat sensitivity analysis gave similar results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Identity of study medication was blinded, but the volume administered was not blinded to the investigators.

domain_judgments.rationale: Transfusion results were available for 173 of 182 randomized patients in the reported intent-to-treat analysis, with nine excluded because they did not undergo surgery; the modest, somewhat group-imbalanced exclusions could potentially affect the effect estimate, although evaluability rates did not differ significantly.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Nine patients (3 = 300 IU/kg Epoetin alfa, 2 = 150 IU/kg Epoetin alfa, and 4 = placebo) were excluded from the analysis because they did not undergo the scheduled operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome—receipt of allogeneic transfusion—was objective, recorded daily and measured consistently across groups, and medication identity was blinded despite unblinded injection volume.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The number of units of allogeneic blood (ie, whole blood and packed RBCs) transfused was recorded daily starting on the day of operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes and statistical methods are clearly identified, but no protocol, registration, or prespecified analysis plan is cited, and both evaluable-patient and modified intent-to-treat analyses were available, leaving some possibility of selective analysis or reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy variable was the proportion of patients given a transfusion.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. The objective, blinded outcome assessment is reassuring, but allocation concealment was not explicit, the principal analysis excluded randomized participants, some outcome data were unavailable, and no protocol or prespecified analysis plan was reported.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports random assignment of 600 eligible patients using a permuted-block scheme with 1:1 allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: A permuted-block 1:1 randomization scheme was implemented by a study coordinator after consent, assignments were withheld from investigators, and measured baseline characteristics were generally balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A permuted block randomization scheme with 1:1 allocation was used to keep the group sizes equal. Randomization was performed by a study coordinator immediately after consent was obtained but group assignments were not disclosed to the investigators until the study was complete.

domain_judgments.rationale: Clinical staff involved in treatment and outcome evaluation were blinded, both groups received standardized co-interventions, all randomized participants received their assigned treatment, and analyses were intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All investigators, surgeons, anesthesiologists, perfusionists, and intensive care unit physicians responsible for the administration of blood products or involved in the evaluation of outcomes were blinded with respect to group assignment thereby creating a single-blinded study.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 600 randomized participants were analyzed for the primary transfusion outcome, and no surviving participant was lost during the 45-day follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the remaining 600 patients, 300 were allocated to and received HRE and 300 were allocated to the control group... None of the survivors were lost to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objectively recorded, transfusion decisions followed a mandatory uniform hemoglobin threshold, and responsible clinicians and outcome evaluators were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A trigger Hb level of 8.0 g/dL was strictly observed as threshold for transfusions allowing no discretion to physicians.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and its primary and secondary endpoints are identified, but the text does not provide the prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan needed to exclude selective choice among subgroup analyses, outcome definitions, or analytic approaches.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study... was registered at Clinicaltrials.gov with the Clinical Trial Registration Number NCT01265680.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by insufficient information to verify that reported outcomes and analyses—particularly subgroup analyses—were fully prespecified. Randomization, blinding of clinical/outcome personnel, complete outcome ascertainment, standardized transfusion criteria, and intention-to-treat analysis otherwise support low risk across the remaining domains.

design_rationale: The trial explicitly used a computer-generated 1:1 randomization schema, stratified by planned TAVI route.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, stratified by planned access route, and implemented by an independent technician, with investigators blinded to assignments; the isolated baseline haemoglobin imbalance is plausibly due to chance and was adjusted for.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were assigned to receive EPO (+iron) or placebo using a computer-generated randomisation schema in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by planned route... Randomisation was performed by a technician who was not otherwise involved in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators were blinded and adherence was nearly complete, but four randomized participants were excluded from analysis after treatment and the analysis was therefore not fully intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two patients receiving EPO and one patient receiving placebo infusions did not finally undergo TAVI and were excluded from the analyses. One additional patient was excluded due to active bleeding before TAVI.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 100 participants retained in the analysis had 30-day follow-up, with no losses reported; post-randomization exclusions were few and balanced enough to be unlikely to materially bias the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were followed for 30 days and no patients were lost at follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Red-cell transfusion was an objective outcome governed by prespecified clinical thresholds, assessed under blinded conditions, and independently confirmed against blinded blood-bank records.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data regarding RC transfusions were further confirmed using the data from the local blood bank (Héma-Québec, Canada), which was blinded regarding treatment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary outcome was clearly specified, but the provided report does not establish that a prespecified statistical analysis plan was finalized before unblinding, and several adjusted, time-to-event, landmark, and subgroup analyses permit some analytical flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02390102

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. Randomization, blinding, outcome ascertainment, and follow-up were strong, but the exclusion of four randomized and treated participants meant the analysis was not fully intention-to-treat, and the available report does not confirm a prespecified analysis plan sufficient to rule out selective analytical reporting.
